hero.eyebrow: Blockchain & Web3 · No coding, no wallet needed
hero.title: Blockchain & Web3: learn it by breaking it
hero.subtitle: Hash text, tamper with a live chain and re-mine it, work out Bitcoin's supply and Ethereum fees in a working spreadsheet, and learn to judge projects and stay safe. Every task is checked and explained.
hero.outcomeLine: After this course you can explain how blockchains work, judge whether a project needs one and protect yourself from scams.

Pass each module quiz (70% or more). Short tests inside the lessons give instant feedback.
Complete the use-case brief and the final assessment.

faq.q: Do I need to code or own any crypto?
faq.a: No. Everything runs in your browser. The course never asks you to buy anything, and it recommends test networks if you want to experiment later.
No. It is education. Crypto assets are risky and rules differ by country, so ask a qualified professional before investing.

faq.q: Will it make me a developer?
faq.a: It builds the foundation. The Ethereum and Solidity courses in this series go on to writing smart contracts.

activities.title: Bitcoin's halving schedule
activities.objective: Calculate how many coins each era creates and show that supply approaches a fixed cap.
activities.scenario: Bitcoin's block reward started at 50 coins and halves every 210,000 blocks. Work out the coins issued in each era and the running total.
steps: In B3 enter the reward for era 2: half of the reward above it (B2 divided by 2). Fill down to B9.
In C2 work out the coins issued in era 1: the reward in B2 times the blocks per era in B12 (lock B12). Fill down to C9.
In D2 enter the running total: =C2, then in D3 add the previous total and C3. Fill down to D9.
In B13 show how far the supply is from the 21,000,000 cap after eight eras: the cap in B14 minus D9.

checks.label: B3 halves the reward
checks.hint: Divide the reward above by 2.
checks.explain: Each era pays half the previous reward.

checks.label: B9 is the era-8 reward
checks.hint: Fill down.

checks.label: C2 is era 1's issuance
D3 is the running total after era 2
checks.explain: Add each era to the total so far.

checks.label: D9 is the total after eight eras
checks.hint: Fill down.
checks.explain: It gets very close to the cap.

checks.label: B13 is what is left to issue

cells.A13: Still to be issued after era 8

activities.title: What does a transaction cost?
activities.objective: Calculate a network fee from gas used and gas price, and compare costs when the network is busy.
activities.scenario: On Ethereum a fee equals the gas a transaction uses times the price per unit of gas. A simple transfer uses 21,000 gas. Gas prices are quoted in gwei, and 1 ETH is 1,000,000,000 gwei. Compare a quiet and a busy moment (the ETH price is illustrative).
steps: In C2 work out the fee in gwei: gas used times gas price (B2 times the price in row 2's column). Use B7 for gas used.
In D2 convert to ETH: gwei divided by 1,000,000,000.
In E2 convert to rupees: ETH times the rupee price in B8.
Fill rows 2 to 4.
In B10 work out how many times more expensive the busiest moment is than the quietest: E4 divided by E2.

checks.label: C2 is the fee in gwei
D2 is the fee in ETH
E2 is the fee in rupees
E4 is the busy-moment fee
checks.hint: Fill down.
checks.explain: The same steps for the busy row.

checks.label: B10 compares busy with quiet
checks.explain: Divide the busy fee by the quiet fee.

cells.A7: Gas used by a simple transfer
